_why_no_distinguished_by: `BoingBag3.9-3&4` is this archive's own single top-level directory and no
other archive in the owner's folder claims it. A condition that separates
nothing can only refuse an archive that would have worked.
_why_chain_position_and_requires: 8 - last, and the readme says why: `Requires: OS3.9+BB2`, and the Install
script's own `#msg-bad-revision` refuses a tree that has not had BoingBags
BoingBag 3.9-1 - and naming both here would state one fact twice.
The readme also states what goes on *before* it and is not incorporated:
*"The various BB2 Locale packages ... are not incorporated. You should
install any of them that you require before installing BB3&4."* That is
the group at ranks 4 to 7, and it is expressed as their ranks rather than
as a `requires` here: they are optional, and a `requires` naming an
optional package would refuse a chain nobody has to install.
_why_host_placement_block_needs_installe: **Not an encryption block - a decision block.** Nothing in this archive is
encrypted; every one of the 983 entries is a plain file. What ART cannot do
is *decide*, and its own `Install` script is 1600 lines of deciding. Read in
full on 2026-09-08, it:
- asks `askoptions` which languages to install and copies only those;
- copies `Files1` whole into the volume root, and `Files3` only if the
user asked for the optional contributions;
- picks the 060, 040 or 020 build of `xadmaster.library`, `mpega*.library`
and the BMP/PNG datatypes from the CPU it detects;
- copies one of five `scsi-A<model>.device` files under the name
`scsi.device`, chosen by the machine the user names;
- copies into whatever `AmiTCP:` and `SYS:Internet/AWeb3SE` happen to be,
renaming and deleting inside them first;
- deletes `L/CrossDOSFileSystem` from the target;
- renames files inside its own source drawer;
- runs `Files2/C/FixFonts` after the fonts, which ART cannot do
(`euro-update.json` carries that measurement in full);
- and offers to open `SYS:Tools/EditPad` on the startup-sequence.
A `PathRule` set cannot express any of that. Declaring the unconditional
half as if it were the whole would produce a tree that boots and is quietly
short of the components it thinks it has - this project's named defect - so
the row is refused for host placement and says why.
_why_amiga_installer_and_not_yet_runnabl: **The declaration is honest about what it is not.** `program` names
`Install`, the archive's own Installer script - the artefact that installs
this package - and `Install` is a *script*, not a program: it has to be
handed to `C:Installer` on the target, and ART's engine launches a program
with fixed arguments. So the declaration cannot be composed into a run as
it stands, and `not_yet_runnable` is exactly that gap, written down where
the screen can read it.
It is not left out. Omitting `amiga_installer` would make
`PackageSummary::amigaInstallable` false and the row would vanish from the
Amiga-side panel entirely - ART silently claiming it ships nothing for a
package it ships a whole recipe for. Section 10's rule is the opposite:
register the unready action and say why it is unready. The panel renders
the row disabled with this sentence, and `commands::amigainstall::compose`
refuses a request for it whatever the screen does.
**What would have to be measured.** Whether `Installer` can drive this
script unattended at all. The script sets `(user N)` internally, asks
`askoptions` for the languages and `confirm`s the target, and none of the
AmigaOS 3.9 Installer scripts accepts `NOVICE`, `DEFUSER`, `LOGFILE`,
`MINUSER` or `PROMPTUSER` (research section 2). Round 3's task 3 is where
that is run and counted; until then this row is a question ART is asking,
not a promise it is making.

amiga_installer.not_yet_runnable: the Installer script has not been run unattended by ART; round 3 task 3 measures it

_why_overrides: Every path the rules below name is one `workbench-base` and `workbench-39`
already write, and BoingBags 3&4 replaces them on purpose - which is what
an update is. `boingbag-39-1` and `boingbag-39-2` are named too, since this
goes on after both and replaces what they left. The declaration is what
separates a deliberate layer from a package that landed on a name nobody
expected; `boingbag-39-1.json` records the reasoning at length.
_why_rules_are_the_unconditional_copies_: **These rules are documentation, not a placement plan**, and
`host_placement_block` above is what stops them being applied. They are the
copies the script makes with no question asked - `Files2/Devs/Keymaps`,
root, written out as its twelve own drawers because a rule's destination
may not be empty. Everything conditional is deliberately absent rather than
guessed at: see the block's own note for the list.
